items.question: How is the scripture divided and how does the being of knowledge unfold?
premises: The scripture named Rudra, Shiva, and Bhairava is established threefold.
This division holds in reality, not merely conventionally.
The being of knowledge itself unfolds in a threefold way.
items.inference: The threefold division of the scripture corresponds to a real threefold unfolding of the being of knowledge.
items.plain_english: Thus the scripture, named Rudra, Shiva, and Bhairava, is established as threefold in reality; for indeed this being of knowledge unfolds in a threefold way.

rows.grounds: fused form: pūrṇena + abheda-sandhinā; third mode

items.question: What are the three modes by which knowledge unfolds and which powers correspond to them?
premises: Knowledge unfolds by difference, by difference-and-nondifference, and by the full junction of nondifference.
There are three principal powers belonging to Shambhu.
These powers begin with will and correspond to the three modes.
items.inference: The three principal Shambhu powers of will and so on correspond to the three modes of difference, mixed difference-nondifference, and full nondifference.
items.plain_english: It unfolds by difference, by difference-and-nondifference, and by the full junction of nondifference; and likewise there are three principal powers of Shambhu, beginning with will.

rows.grounds: fused form: tatra + eva; locative emphasis

items.question: How does the elaboration of the five powers relate to the supreme triad?
premises: In that same context there is an elaboration involving the five powers and so on.
In the middle that triad appears divided.
Even so, that triad is indeed supreme.
items.inference: The elaboration into five powers occurs within the triad, yet the triad remains the supreme reality.
items.plain_english: There indeed, by elaboration, there is the application of the five powers and so on; thus, though divided in the middle, that triad is indeed supreme.

rows.grounds: genitive dual of the two streams

items.question: How is this scripture established in the teacher's lineage and why is it near the left and right streams?
premises: The scripture is established in our teacher's house through the sequence of transmission.
Its position follows from nearness to the left and right scriptures.
This nearness explains its particular placement in the tradition.
items.inference: The scripture's transmission in the teacher's lineage is grounded in its proximity to the left and right scriptural streams.
items.plain_english: The scripture is established in our teacher's house through the lineage sequence; therefore, indeed, because of its nearness to the left and right scriptures.

items.question: Where does the Kaula stream unfold and what state arises from it?
premises: The Kaula stream fully unfolds at the edge of the edge-stream.
From that unfolding arises a state beyond limiting conditions.
In that state all limitations of beings are withdrawn and fullness remains.
items.inference: The Kaula stream unfolds at the outermost edge and leads to a fullness in which all limiting conditions of beings are withdrawn.
items.plain_english: The Kaula stream fully unfolds at the edge of the edge-stream; and from that, full with all the limiting conditions of beings withdrawn.

rows.grounds: describes the range of the triad
fused form: kroḍīkṛtya + avatiṣṭhate; main action

items.question: How does Bhairava abide in relation to the three powers across the channels?
premises: Bhairava's activity is expanded by the rising fluid of supreme reality.
In the Ishana, left, and right channels the triad of powers appears in sequence.
Bhairava embraces that triad from Apara up to Para and abides.
items.inference: Bhairava abides as the encompassing reality that holds the full triad of powers across the three channels from Apara to Para.
items.plain_english: Bhairava, whose activity is expanded by the rising fluid of supreme reality, embraces the triad of powers in sequence in those Ishana, left, and right channels, from Apara up to Para, and abides.

items.question: How is the supreme lord described in relation to division and reabsorption?
premises: That principle manifests the division of difference and makes it clear.
The same supreme lord is infinite and about to reabsorb that division.
In reality the tradition declares that supreme form to be three-headed.
items.inference: The supreme lord both manifests differentiated division and reabsorbs it, and is therefore declared in reality to be three-headed.
items.plain_english: It manifests that division of difference and makes it clear; and then they declare that infinite, reabsorbing form of the supreme lord to be, in reality, truly three-headed.

items.question: Why are the upper, left, and other tantras and kulas established in that stream?
premises: The upper, left, and other tantras and kulas are established in that stream.
Their establishment serves a specific purpose.
That purpose is the removal of the contraction caused by difference.
items.inference: The various tantras and kulas are grounded in that stream in order to remove the contraction produced by difference.
items.plain_english: The upper, left, and other tantras and kulas are established in that stream for the removal of the contraction of difference.

items.question: What is the nature of scriptural meanings that are accessible to the world?
premises: Scriptural meanings rest on Maya-born Vaikhari speech heard by all.
They take the form of letters, sentences, and words.
Such meanings fall within the range of ordinary worldly cognition.
items.inference: The scriptural meanings accessible to the world are those expressed through Maya-born Vaikhari speech in the form of letters, sentences, and words.
items.plain_english: The scriptural meanings that rest on Maya-born Vaikhari speech heard by all, and whose nature is letters, sentences, and words, are within the range of the world.

rows.grounds: metaphor for the level of Vaikhari

items.question: Through what level of speech do scriptural meanings proceed to the transmitters of the tantras?
premises: Scriptural meanings proceed by resorting to the various transmitters of the tantras.
This transmission occurs first at the level of Maya-born Vaikhari.
Vaikhari is described as a cavity or channel through which the meaning comes down.
items.inference: The descent of scriptural meaning to the transmitters of the tantras first passes through the Maya-born level of Vaikhari speech.
items.plain_english: Having resorted to those various transmitters of the tantras, they proceed; therefore, at first, as long as they come through the Maya-born cavity of Vaikhari.

rows.grounds: fused form: na + ayam; negated subject

items.question: Does scriptural meaning bound by Maya-born letters reach the inner supreme speech?
premises: Scriptural meaning can be bound by Maya-born letters.
The inner level consists of supreme speech letters of essential awakening.
Meaning in that outer form does not arrive at that inner level.
items.inference: Scriptural meaning confined to Maya-born letters does not reach the inner essence of supreme speech.
items.plain_english: This scriptural meaning, bound by Maya-born letters, has not arrived within as that which consists of the supreme speech-letters of essential awakening.

rows.grounds: fused form: laukika + antaḥ; describes scope

items.question: Where does the scriptural meaning refined by supreme immersion ultimately abide?
premises: Scriptural meaning can be refined by the root impression of uncontrived supreme immersion.
Such meaning extends even to the worldly level.
Its true locus is the supreme lord, the thirty-seventh principle.
items.inference: The scriptural meaning rooted in uncontrived supreme immersion, though reaching the worldly level, abides in the supreme thirty-seventh lord.
uncertainties: The exact referent of 'thirty-seventh' follows the Śaiva tattva scheme but is not glossed in the verse itself.
items.plain_english: The scriptural meaning, refined by the root impression of uncontrived supreme immersion, extends to the worldly level, yet it is in the supreme thirty-seventh lord.

rows.grounds: fused form: tatra + asatām; genitive plural
fused form: kva + api; indefinite locative
fused form: na + asti; negated existence

items.question: Can unreal beings possess reality or can respect arise in a nature overcome by disrespect?
premises: Unreal beings have no reality anywhere at all.
A nature overcome by disrespect is opposed to respect.
Respect cannot arise where its opposing condition dominates.
items.inference: Just as unreal beings lack reality, respect cannot arise in a nature overcome by disrespect.
items.plain_english: For there, unreal beings have no reality anywhere at all; how could respect arise in a lordly nature overcome by disrespect?

items.question: What is the ultimate status of all scriptural meaning and of the Vedas and other teachings?
premises: The entire meaning of scripture is established as the nature of the supreme principle.
The Vedas and other teachings appear as distinct scriptural portions.
Those portions belong to the Maya-born level of expression.
items.inference: All scriptural meaning is grounded in the supreme principle, while the Vedas and other teachings are Maya-born portions of that teaching.
items.plain_english: Therefore the entire meaning of scripture is established as the nature of the supreme principle; hence even these Vedas and others are Maya-born portions of teaching.

rows.grounds: fused form: na + anyataḥ; negated alternative source

items.question: From what source do the teachings shine forth and can there be any other cause?
premises: The teachings shine forth from the power of the Bhairava-sun alone.
No other source accounts for their manifestation.
Apart from the reflective awareness of consciousness there can be no other cause anywhere.
items.inference: The teachings manifest solely from the reflective awareness of consciousness, symbolized as the power of the Bhairava-sun.
items.plain_english: They shine forth from the power of the Bhairava-sun alone, not from elsewhere; for apart from the reflective awareness of consciousness there could be no other cause anywhere at all.

rows.grounds: fused form: ca + iti; quotation marker

items.question: Why can consciousness be spoken of as both cause and effect?
premises: The consciousness of the lord of consciousness is nothing other than consciousness itself.
The terms effect and cause are applied to it.
This application is figurative rather than a real division.
items.inference: Because consciousness remains only consciousness, the distinction between cause and effect is applied to it only figuratively.
items.plain_english: The consciousness of the lord of consciousness would be consciousness alone; therefore, since it is spoken of as both effect and cause, that status is applied only figuratively.

rows.grounds: fused form: rūpatvena + avabhāsate; main verb

items.question: What appears as the true form of a being through sequential transformation?
premises: A being undergoes transformation in sequence and displays extended properties.
Such transformation has a beginning and an end.
At both beginning and end, consciousness alone appears as its form.
items.inference: Throughout the sequential transformation of a being, consciousness alone is what appears as its true form at beginning and end.
items.plain_english: For in the sequential transformation of a being with extended properties, at the beginning and at the end, consciousness alone appears as its very form.

items.question: What absurd consequence follows if consciousness were subject to division by time?
premises: The verse considers the hypothesis that consciousness endures division by time.
If that were so, an impossible consequence would follow.
The consequence is as absurd as enjoying gravel bits of sky cut by a sharpened sword.
items.inference: Consciousness cannot be subject to division by time, because that hypothesis leads to an absurd impossibility.
items.plain_english: And if consciousness could endure division by time, then we would clearly be enjoying gravel bits of sky cut by a sharpened sword.

items.question: Why are all the scriptures self-luminous in reality?
premises: All the scriptures do not fall away from the form of consciousness.
Consciousness is self-luminous.
What does not fall away from self-luminous consciousness shares that luminosity.
items.inference: Because all scriptures remain within the form of self-luminous consciousness, they are in reality self-luminous.
items.plain_english: Therefore all the scriptures, because they do not fall away from the form of consciousness and because consciousness is self-luminous, are in reality self-luminous.

items.question: Can the expressed meaning ever stand apart from the expressing word?
premises: One might object that the expressed stands apart from the expresser.
By its autonomy the expresser alone appears as what will be expressed.
Therefore the expressed does not exist as a separate independent entity.
items.inference: The expressed meaning never stands apart from the expresser, because the autonomous expresser itself appears as the future expressed.
items.plain_english: And it should not be said that the expressed ever stands apart from the expresser; for by autonomy the expresser alone appears as what will be expressed.

items.question: In what different ways can the expressing aspect of a word appear?
premises: The expressing aspect of a word does not appear in only one fixed mode.
Sometimes it appears with the expressed absorbed into its own nature.
Sometimes it appears as expressing only a general flash of meaning.
items.inference: The expressing aspect of speech appears in varying modes, either absorbing the expressed into itself or presenting only a general meaning.
items.plain_english: Sometimes the expressing aspect appears with the expressed absorbed into its own nature; sometimes, instead, it appears as expressing a general flash.

items.question: How does a word appear when its expressed aspect becomes fully clear?
premises: A word can appear qualified by near and countless qualifiers.
Its expressed aspect can surge forth clearly.
In that mode the word shines with a clear expressed aspect of its own form.
items.inference: At times a word shines forth with a clear surge of its expressed aspect, qualified by many determinations.
items.plain_english: Sometimes it shines, qualified by near and countless qualifiers, with a surge of the clear expressed aspect of its own form.

rows.grounds: fused form: kva + api; indefinite locative

items.question: What different orientations can arise in the state of words and meaning?
premises: Words can be oriented toward meaning or toward their own form.
At times the meaning is what one desires to know.
At times the state becomes one consisting of rasa.
items.inference: The manifestation of words varies between orientation toward meaning, orientation toward their own form, a desire to know meaning, and a rasa-filled state.
items.plain_english: Therefore sometimes there is orientation toward meaning, and likewise sometimes orientation toward the word's own form; sometimes a state in which the meaning is desired to be known, and sometimes a state consisting of rasa.

rows.grounds: fused form: kacati + iti; explanatory clause

items.question: Why is the variegated appearance of words not surprising?
premises: Words display a variegated range of states.
They never depart from the form of consciousness.
Consciousness itself flashes forth in varied ways.
items.inference: The variegated appearance of words is unsurprising because it arises from the varied flashings of consciousness while never departing from consciousness.
items.plain_english: A variegated state of words is observed, because they do not depart from the form of consciousness; since it flashes through the varied flashings of consciousness, what is wonderful about that?
